title: Comparison of the Safety and Efficacy of Remimazolam for Sedation in Adults Undergoing Fiberoptic Bronchoscopy: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
authors: Lee S, Na HS, Koo BW, Joo DH, Shin HJ
abstract: BACKGROUND: Fiberoptic bronchoscopy requires effective sedation to ensure patient comfort while preserving gas exchange, hemodynamic stability, and predictable recovery. Remimazolam, a novel ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine, has emerged as a potential alternative to traditional sedatives. However, its safety and efficacy compared with those of other sedatives remain under investigation. This meta-analysis evaluated the safety and efficacy of remimazolam versus dexmedetomidine, midazolam, and propofol in adults undergoing fiberoptic bronchoscopy. METHODS: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted using 5 databases through January 2026. Outcomes included respiratory depression, hypotension, bradycardia, time to target sedation depth, procedure success rate, emergence time, and postanesthesia care unit (PACU) stay. Relative risks (RR) or mean differences (MD) with 95% CI were calculated using a random-effects model. RESULTS: Sixteen RCTs (2325 patients) were included. Remimazolam significantly reduced respiratory depression (RR: 0.51, 95% CI: 0.36-0.73, P<0.001), hypotension (RR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.34-0.73, P<0.001), and bradycardia (RR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.22-0.65, P=0.001) versus controls. Sedation onset was faster than dexmedetomidine (MD: -2.19 min), but slower than propofol (MD: 0.49 min). Success rates were comparable across groups (RR: 1.12, 95% CI: 0.98-1.28, P=0.097). Compared with dexmedetomidine and midazolam, remimazolam shortened emergence (MD: -1.79 and -4.37 min, respectively) and PACU stay (MD: -3.58 and -6.70 min). CONCLUSION: Remimazolam provides effective sedation for fiberoptic bronchoscopy with advantages in terms of respiratory and hemodynamic safety, rapid recovery, and procedural efficiency.

title: Prediction Models for Delayed Bleeding After Colorectal Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal.
authors: Miao D, Hou Z, Ge Y, Qi H
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although many predictive models have been developed or validated for delayed bleeding after colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD), their methodological quality and clinical utility remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed and critically appraised all available predictive models for this outcome. METHODS: We searched five databases through March 2026 for observational studies that developed or validated prediction models or scoring systems for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD in adults (≥18 years). Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using PROBAST. RESULTS: Of 25,177 records screened, five studies reporting five predictive models were included. The incidence of delayed bleeding ranged from 2.9% to 9.9%. The most commonly used predictors were lesion location and lesion size. Discrimination in derivation cohorts ranged from 0.726 to 0.890, internal validation areas under the curve [AUCs] ranged from 0.739 to 0.870, and the externally validated model achieved an AUC of 0.634. All studies were judged to have a high risk of bias, mainly because of inadequate reporting in the predictor, outcome, and analysis domains, although most had low concerns regarding applicability. CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review identified five predictive models for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD. Lesion location and size were the most frequently reported predictors. Discriminative performance varied across derivation and validation cohorts, with suboptimal external-validation results. All models had a high risk of bias per PROBAST (low concerns regarding applicability); therefore, their findings should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Endobronchial Valves for Persistent Air Leak and Bronchopleural Fistula in Children: A Systematic Review of Indications, Procedural Approaches, and Outcomes.
authors: Mahindrakar N, Bhandari P, Yedatore R, Vorakunthada Y, Lilitwat W
abstract: BACKGROUND: Persistent air leak (PAL) and bronchopleural fistula (BPF) are uncommon but important complications in children, particularly with necrotizing pneumonia, postoperative injury, malignancy, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). When conservative therapy fails or surgery is high-risk, endobronchial or intrabronchial valve placement has emerged as a minimally invasive bronchoscopic option. This systematic review summarizes the published pediatric experience, focusing on indications, procedural approach, and outcomes. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to June 2026, with Google Scholar and reference lists screened; no language limits applied. Eligible studies reported pediatric or late-adolescent patients who underwent bronchoscopic valve placement for PAL, BPF, or pneumothorax with ongoing air leak. Case reports, case series, and observational studies with extractable pediatric data were included. Two reviewers independently screened, assessed eligibility, and abstracted data; findings were synthesized narratively. RESULTS: Thirteen reports were included. Valve placement achieved rapid or eventual air-leak improvement in selected children, including those with necrotizing pneumonia, postoperative air leak, chronic ventilator dependence, malignancy, and ECMO support. Reported complications included valve migration or loosening, granulation tissue, minor hemoptysis, atelectasis, contralateral pneumothorax, and recurrent air leak, although many children underwent valve removal without complication. CONCLUSION: Endobronchial or intrabronchial valve placement may be a useful rescue or bridge therapy for carefully selected children with refractory PAL or BPF. Evidence remains low certainty owing to small samples, retrospective design, inconsistent outcome definitions, and possible publication bias. Prospective multicenter registries with standardized reporting are needed to define optimal selection, timing, and safety.

title: Randomized controlled trials of radiation therapy for cutaneous malignancies: a systematic review.
authors: Mahase SS, Miccio J, Chilov M, Gharzai LA, Barker CA, Zaorsky NG
abstract: PURPOSE: In cutaneous oncology, radiotherapy use is largely based on retrospective studies, institutional experience, and expert consensus, with limited high-level evidence to guide practice. We summarize randomized controlled trials in cutaneous radiation oncology and identify gaps in contemporary treatment warranting additional study. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We searched Ovid MEDLINE ALL, Embase.com, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials for randomized controlled trials of radiotherapy for cutaneous malignancies: basal cell carcinoma (BCC), squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), melanoma, and Merkel cell carcinoma. Outcomes of interest included recurrence, survival, toxicity and cosmesis. Study inclusion required approval by three authors, with discrepancies resolved by an additional author. RESULTS: Thirteen trials entailing fewer than 2500 patients were identified, with only four studies published in the last decade. Three BCC studies compared radiotherapy with other treatments, while two additional BCC studies and one mixed BCC/SCC study compared dose-fractionation regimens. One SCC study evaluated adjuvant radiotherapy versus chemoradiotherapy. Among five melanoma trials, four evaluated adjuvant radiotherapy, including one for the primary tumor site and three for the regional nodal basin, and one compared definitive radiotherapy with topical imiquimod for unresectable melanoma in situ. One Merkel cell carcinoma trial evaluated lymph node basin radiotherapy. CONCLUSIONS: Randomized trials of radiotherapy for cutaneous malignancies are limited, small and heterogeneous, relative to the frequency of these diseases and clinical trials of other therapeutic interventions. Modern randomized trials are needed to bridge these gaps.

title: Effects on health and antioxidant status of oral supplementation of hazelnut skin extract in dairy calves with neonatal diarrhea: a randomized clinical trial in hospitalized patients.
authors: Boccardo A, Sannazzaro M, Sala G, Gazzola E, Martucci I, Curone G, Castrica M, Ferrulli V
abstract: Neonatal calf diarrhea (NCD) is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality in calves. Growing concern about antimicrobial resistance has spurred interest in phytotherapeutic alternatives, particularly polyphenol-rich extracts. Hazelnut skin (HS), a by-product of the confectionery sector, is a sustainable and underutilized source of polyphenols; however, its therapeutic efficacy in calves with NCD remains insufficiently investigated. This randomized, parallel-group clinical trial evaluated the effects of oral HS extract supplementation as an adjunct to standard medical therapy in hospitalized dairy calves with NCD. Sixty female Holstein calves were randomly allocated to a control group (CTRL; n = 30) or a treatment group (HS; n = 30) receiving 10 g/day of HS extract with milk for 5 days. All calves received standardized clinical management, including fluid therapy and antimicrobial administration. Clinical parameters, milk intake, body weight, hospitalization outcomes, sepsis scores, and blood oxidative stress biomarkers were monitored. No significant differences were detected between groups for clinical recovery, fecal score, hydration status, milk intake, weight gain, hospitalization duration, mortality, or oxidative stress markers. Clinical improvement over time was evident in both groups and was attributable to standard therapy. In conclusion, short-term oral supplementation with HS extract did not confer additional clinical or antioxidant benefits when added to conventional treatment in calves with NCD.

title: Metformin Use Is Associated With Reduced Rates of Primary Nerve Decompression Surgery and Revision in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authors: Abbas Y, Kucharski A, Boukind A, Wright D, Dy CJ, Brogan DM
journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
abstract: PURPOSE: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is a risk factor for compressive neuropathy. The purpose of this study was to determine whether metformin use is associated with reduced rates of compressive neuropathy, primary nerve decompression surgery, and revision after carpal tunnel release and cubital tunnel release, while controlling for concurrent diabetes medications. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX federated research network. Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus were stratified by metformin exposure, defined as at least 10 prescriptions over 5 years. The primary outcomes were incident compressive neuropathy and nerve decompression surgery. In a unilateral revision cohort, the outcome was ipsilateral revision between 30 days and 5 years after the index procedure. One-to-one propensity score matching balanced cohorts on demographics, comorbidities, and concurrent diabetes medications. Four prespecified medication-stratified sensitivity analyses addressed insulin, sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists. Carpal tunnel release and cubital tunnel release revision results were pooled via fixed-effect meta-analysis. RESULTS: After matching, the primary analysis included 260,823 pairs. Metformin users had lower rates of nerve decompression surgery (0.60% vs 0.72%; odds ratio, OR, 0.831 [0.776-0.889]) and compressive neuropathy diagnosis (2.78% vs 3.05%; OR, 0.909 [0.879-0.941]). The surgery-level association was stronger without concurrent insulin (OR, 0.727 [0.662-0.799]) and attenuated to nonsignificance with concurrent insulin (OR, 0.948 [0.836-1.076]), though the diagnosis-level association persisted. Among patients with unilateral carpal or cubital tunnel syndrome, ipsilateral revision was less frequent in metformin users (pooled OR, 0.711 [0.533-0.950]). Metformin users also had lower vitamin B12 levels (mean, 646.4 vs 707.4 pg/mL), consistent with sustained metformin exposure. CONCLUSIONS: Metformin use was associated with reduced incidence of nerve decompression surgery and ipsilateral revision after carpal tunnel release and cubital tunnel release in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, with directionally consistent effects across sensitivity analyses. These findings suggest that maintaining metformin therapy may carry benefit beyond glycemic control. Prospective studies are needed to validate these findings. TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic II.

title: Advanced cell-instructive bio-inks: Engineering multiscale niches for functional tissue formation.
authors: Ng WL, Xu Y, Liu F, Bartolo P
abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has transformed tissue fabrication by enabling the precise spatial organization of living cells and biomaterials into biomimetic tissue constructs. However, advances in manufacturing have outpaced the development of bio-inks capable of actively directing tissue formation. Most existing bio-inks remain optimized for printability, rheological behaviour, and structural fidelity, while providing limited control over the biological processes that govern tissue morphogenesis, functional maturation, and regeneration. This review examines the emerging paradigm of cell-instructive bio-inks, which integrate biological regulation directly into material design to recreate the cellular microenvironments that guide tissue development. We present a unifying framework that classifies these bio-inks according to three complementary regulatory dimensions: biochemical niches that regulate cell fate through molecular signalling and regenerative matrices; architectural niches that direct tissue organization through spatial and structural cues; and metabolic niches that modulate oxygen availability, redox homeostasis, and cellular metabolism. We further discuss strategies for integrating these instructive functions within multifunctional bio-inks, together with scalable manufacturing, and artificial intelligence-assisted bio-ink design. By redefining bio-inks as active regulators of cellular behaviour, this review establishes a conceptual framework for engineering next-generation bio-inks capable of orchestrating tissue development, functional maturation, and regenerative outcomes.

title: Machine learning algorithms empower traditional Chinese medicine: Breakthrough approaches from chemical component analysis to pharmacological mechanism research.
authors: Han Z, Zhao F, Xu H, Zhang Z, Wu J, Zhang Y, Pan J, Li M
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine studies are constrained by complex chemical components and multi-target biological interactions, making conventional analytical methods inefficient for mechanism exploration. As a data-driven technique, machine learning has been widely adopted to tackle diverse complex challenges in TCM research. Nevertheless, most existing reviews merely summarize individual algorithms or scattered application cases, lacking systematic task-based classification and unified operational standards. Based on literature published from 2022 to 2026, this review systematically classifies machine learning applications in TCM into four core research tasks. A task-oriented framework is constructed to match different algorithms with appropriate TCM research scenarios. This paper further establishes a complete standardized workflow covering algorithm selection, model construction and model evaluation to standardize ML applications in TCM research. This review also summarizes the applications of machine learning in TCM quality control, bioactive compound identification, processing analysis, and mechanism elucidation. Furthermore, major bottlenecks in current ML-based TCM studies are analyzed, and feasible optimization strategies are proposed. This review aims to provide clear and practical guidelines for the standardized application of machine learning in future TCM research.

title: Artificial Intelligence in suicide prevention: promise, peril, and clinical implications for clinical practice.
authors: Nobile B, Courtet P
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into psychiatry is progressing rapidly, with promising yet underexplored applications in suicide prevention. While most existing studies have focused on suicide risk prediction, AI could be applied more broadly across the suicide prevention continuum. This review explores AI's potential in improving the detection of suicidal ideation (SI), enhancing clinician training, and expanding patient access to psychotherapeutic support. Studies suggest that AI models may identify SI more sensitively than clinicians by detecting subtle linguistic or semantic cues. Furthermore, AI-based virtual patients have been shown to improve clinicians' confidence and accuracy in suicide risk assessments, particularly when used alongside traditional training methods. On the patient side, CBT-inspired AI tools offer scalable, on-demand support, but most remain unregulated and clinically unvalidated. Despite their perceived empathy and availability, such tools pose ethical and clinical risks. Many patients use AI tools without professional guidance, a trend clinicians often underestimate. This disconnect calls for urgent regulatory oversight and professional engagement. Without clear clinical validation, AI-based tools may evolve outside medical frameworks, exposing vulnerable individuals to preventable harm. Psychiatry must not only adapt but also lead, ensuring that innovation is harnessed responsibly to serve patients with empathy, safety, and scientific rigor.

title: Microenvironmental barriers to healing in osteoradionecrosis and opportunities for regenerative intervention.
authors: La Croix AE, Torres Gouveia ME, Bertone PM, Nemanic NM, Bahney CS, Hixon KR
abstract: Osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is a debilitating sequela of radiotherapy (RT) for head and neck cancer (HNC), characterized by persistent bone exposure or radiographic non-viability and profound tissue repair failure. Despite advances in radiation delivery and clinical management, ORN remains challenging to treat, with therapeutic strategies largely focused on symptom control, infection mitigation, or surgical reconstruction rather than restoration of regenerative capacity. Emerging evidence suggests that radiation-induced cellular senescence represents a central and underrecognized driver of ORN pathophysiology. Ionizing radiation disrupts the bone microenvironment through sustained vascular injury, impaired osteogenic-angiogenic coupling, chronic inflammation, and the accumulation of senescent bone-resident and stromal cells that secrete a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Together, these changes create a hostile niche that suppresses bone remodeling and wound healing long after radiation exposure. This review synthesizes current understanding of radiation-induced injury to the bone microenvironment, critically evaluates existing classification systems and treatment strategies for ORN, and examines emerging regenerative approaches. We further propose senotherapeutic strategies targeting radiation-induced cellular senescence as a complementary and potentially transformative avenue to restore tissue repair capacity. By integrating regenerative biomaterials with targeted modulation of senescence, future therapies may move beyond palliation toward true biological resolution of ORN. Biomaterial delivery systems (e.g., injectable hydrogels, mineral composite scaffolds, and cryogel platforms) are emerging as promising vehicles for spatiotemporally controlled senotherapeutic delivery within the irradiated bone niche.

title: Designing sero-epidemiological studies to explore immune markers associated with a reduced risk of invasive Klebsiella pneumoniae disease.
authors: Dangor Z, Balasubramanian R, Izu A, Olwagen C, Le Doare K, Berkley JA, Goldblatt D, Benson N
abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae (Kpn) is a leading cause of neonatal invasive bacterial disease especially in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), with 20-30% of culture-confirmed neonatal sepsis caused by Kpn. This, coupled with the rapid emergence of multidrug-resistant strains, calls for additional therapeutic options. Maternal vaccination represents a promising strategy to confer protection to neonates through transplacental transfer of antibodies, with modelling suggesting a vaccine of moderate efficacy (~70%) could avert over 80,000 neonatal deaths annually. Advancing Kpn vaccine development requires identification and validation of serological thresholds of risk reduction (SToRR), or immune markers associated with a reduced risk of invasive Kpn disease (IKpnD). However, no standardized framework currently exists for this purpose. Drawing on lessons from other pathogens, this review outlines key methodological considerations for designing rigorous sero-epidemiological studies to establish such markers. We address three critical domains: (i) study design and population selection, including the rationale for nested case-control designs within birth cohorts enriched for high-risk neonates; (ii) statistical approaches for threshold estimation, including covariate-adjusted logistic regression and Bayesian frameworks; and (iii) laboratory standardization and assay validation, encompassing binding and functional antibody assays. Addressing these considerations systematically will accelerate the development and deployment of a Kpn vaccine capable of reducing neonatal mortality globally.

title: Targeting the lactate/P300/H3K18la epigenetic pathway with a mechanoadaptive biomimetic hydrogel to suppress traumatic tendon heterotopic ossification.
authors: Feng H, Ang K, Deng Z, Cui C, Chen J, Huang N, Feng Y, Zhang J
abstract: Traumatic heterotopic ossification (HO) is a debilitating complication of tendon injury, yet its pathogenic mechanisms remain elusive and effective preventive strategies are lacking. Here, we identify a glycometabolic-epigenetic axis that drives HO progression. Single-cell profiling and functional analyses reveal that hypoxic chondrocytes undergo glycolytic reprogramming, leading to lactate accumulation and transfer into tendon-derived mesenchymal stem cells (TD-MSCs) through MCT1. This metabolic coupling promotes P300-dependent histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la), activating osteogenic programs characterized by Col6a1, Zhx3, Lox and Vdr expression and thereby facilitating pathological endochondral ossification. Guided by this mechanism, we develop a tendon-adhesive hydrogel (GelHA-A485@Exos) that integrates mechanical repair with targeted epigenetic modulation. MSC-derived exosomes enable localized delivery of the P300 inhibitor A485, suppressing H3K18la and aberrant osteogenic activation, while the hydrogel scaffold enhances tendon regeneration. In vivo and in vitro studies demonstrate that GelHA-A485@Exos promotes tendon healing while preventing HO formation. Our findings establish metabolic-epigenetic communication as a central regulator of traumatic HO and provide a translational therapeutic strategy for its clinical prevention.

title: Error-diagnosis-guided cross-indicator adaptive calibration for near-infrared spectroscopic multi-property prediction of coal quality.
authors: Weng Z, Li J, Yuan L
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) coal-quality datasets often contain many repeated spectra acquired from the same coal samples. Ignoring the coal-sample group structure and indicator-dependent error patterns may compromise the reliability of generalization assessment and calibration stability. To address this issue, this study proposes an error-diagnosis-guided cross-indicator adaptive calibration (ED-CIAC) method for NIRS-based multi-property prediction of coal quality. ED-CIAC performs coal-sample-group-level modeling by robustly aggregating repeated spectra and integrating complementary spectral representations to obtain property-specific base predictions. The remaining prediction errors are characterized across properties and value ranges to identify systematic residual structures. Cross-indicator features constructed from the multi-property base predictions are subsequently introduced as complementary calibration information. Candidate calibrators with direct and residual learning modes are evaluated within each training fold, and the calibrator, learning mode, and correction strength are jointly selected for each property according to internal validation performance. Experiments were conducted on 26 batches of NIRS coal-quality data, including 122,983 repeated spectra from 538 independent coal-sample groups, using coal-sample-group-level fivefold cross-validation. The proposed method achieved R2 values of 0.8717 ± 0.0227, 0.9077 ± 0.0120, 0.8112 ± 0.0460, and 0.9000 ± 0.0157 for total moisture (Mt), dry-basis ash (Ad), dry-basis volatile matter (Vd), and net calorific value as received (Qnet,ar), respectively, outperforming conventional chemometric, machine learning, and literature-based comparison methods. These results demonstrate that group-level multi-view base prediction, residual-guided property-specific calibration, and cross-indicator information utilization can improve the reliability of NIRS-based multi-property coal-quality prediction.

title: Kubelka-Munk theory enhances hyperspectral mineral identification for rock heritage.
authors: Peng L, Yang H, Zhou X, Li X, Ju A, Jiang Z, Yang Y
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Accurate identification of minerals is the fundamental task in the protection of rock cultural relics, directly determining the scientific validity and effectiveness of research on weathering mechanisms, disease prediction, and the development of protective materials. However, remote sensing technology is constrained by spatial and observational conditions, making fine in‑situ surveys difficult to achieve. In contrast, proximal hyperspectral imaging overcomes these limitations, providing a reliable technical foundation and data source for in‑situ mineral detection. In this study, a hyperspectral database of common minerals spanning the 900-1700 nm band was established. The diagnostic spectral features of minerals were enhanced through the integration of Kubelka-Munk theory, while efficient mineral identification was achieved by applying machine learning models. Experimental results indicate that diagnostic spectral characteristics are most pronounced within the 1360-1490 nm band. Performance evaluation shows that average efficiency increased by 12.55% and 28.08%, mean F1 scores improved by 12% and 6.14%, mean Kappa values increased by 10.86% and 4.43%, and the F1score of SVM improved by 30%. In addition, spectral detection was conducted on sandstone samples from the Dazu stone carvings, and the experimental results confirmed the accuracy and reliability of the proposed method.

title: DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel reprograms the immuno-oxidative microenvironment to support stem cell-based cartilage repair in osteoarthritis.
authors: Yu H, Hu Z, Tan Q, Wang C, Wang B, Yan Y, Yu Y, Zhang F
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease, and stem cell therapy is often limited by a hostile joint microenvironment. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and damage-associated cell-free DNA (cfDNA) cooperatively drive innate immune activation, inflammatory macrophage polarization, and chondrogenic instability, forming an immuno-oxidative barrier to cartilage repair. Here, we developed a bioactive DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel (MNKB/HA) to remodel this niche and enhance BMSC-mediated cartilage repair. MNKB/HA integrates Mn3O4 nanozymes with Kartogenin (KGN)-engineered bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) in an injectable hyaluronic acid matrix. Mn3O4 exhibited SOD- and CAT-like activities, scavenging O2·-, H2O2, and ·OH, while efficiently adsorbing cfDNA and CpG-ODN to suppress TLR9/MyD88 signaling and M1 polarization and promote M2 polarization. In vitro, 10 μg/mL Mn3O4 was cytocompatible, protected BMSCs and chondrocytes from H2O2-induced apoptosis, and reshaped inflammatory secretion, with IL-10 increased 8.3-fold and TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β reduced. KGN stabilized the chondrogenic phenotype (SOX9, COL Ⅱ, ACAN), while its combination with Mn3O4 synergistically enhanced chondrogenic stability under oxidative/inflammatory stress. In rat OA, intra-articular MNKB/HA reduced OARSI scores, restored COL II and ACAN, decreased MMP13, improved subchondral bone microarchitecture, and attenuated synovitis and osteophytes. MNKB/HA also reduced synovial cfDNA, weakened TLR9 signaling, promoted M2 polarization, and showed intra-articular retention for at least 10 days without notable systemic toxicity. Thus, MNKB/HA remodels the immuno-oxidative niche through synergistic ROS scavenging and cfDNA adsorption, providing a strategy for stem cell-mediated cartilage repair in OA.

title: From passive fillers to active implants: A 3D-printed trilayer piezoelectric scaffold recapitulating native bone hierarchy.
authors: Shan Y, Li S, Wang Y, Lei Y, Wang G, Zhou Q, Lu Y, Wu Y
abstract: Critical-sized alveolar bone defects affect over 10 million patients annually, yet current synthetic bone substitutes act as passive osteoconductive fillers with unpredictable outcomes. Native bone, by contrast, achieves robust regeneration through a trilayered hierarchy of cancellous, cortical, and metabolically active periosteal tissues, with intrinsic piezoelectricity converting mechanical loading into endogenous electrical cues. While piezoelectric biomaterials have emerged as promising active implants, existing homogeneous scaffolds fail to recapitulate native bone's structural complexity and electromechanical coupling; to date, no work has combined this trilayer architecture with piezoelectric functionality in a single construct. Here we report a trilayer bioinspired piezoelectric scaffold fabricated via a two-step conformal 3D printing strategy, composed of a strontium-doped β-tricalcium phosphate (Sr-β-TCP) triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) cancellous layer, a dense cortical layer, and a barium titanate/silk fibroin (BTO/SF) piezoelectric periosteal layer. Under non-invasive low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) stimulation, the scaffold generates bioelectrical signals that support robust osteogenic activity and pro-angiogenic potential in vitro. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that these electrical cues are associated with intracellular calcium influx and upregulation of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt) and Wnt/β-catenin pathways, consistent with enhanced osteogenic differentiation. In a critical-sized bone defect model, the trilayer scaffold with LIPUS achieves substantially superior bone regeneration relative to controls. This work pioneers the integration of native bone hierarchy with piezoelectric functionality into a single active construct, shifting bone tissue engineering from passive filling to bioelectric-guided repair. Coupling structural biomimicry with electroactive stimulation, this strategy holds potential for future bone regenerative applications, including alveolar bone reconstruction.

title: Tissue engineering polymeric formulations enable lymphangiogenesis for myocardial repair.
authors: Liu Z, Li R, Huang W, Zhang J, Qu Y, Dong W, Liu Y, Li Q
abstract: PURPOSE: Emerging evidence emphasizes the pivotal contribution of cardiac lymphatic activation following ischemic heart injury, with induced lymphangiogenesis driving edema resolution and inflammatory cell clearance. The aim of this study was to identify a bioactive small molecule with pro-lymphangiogenic activity and to develop a tissue engineering polymeric formulation for sustained local delivery in myocardial repair. METHODS: Through a high-throughput screen, we identified the bioactive molecule β-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl) lactic acid (3,4-DHPLA) as a potent stimulator of lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). To leverage this finding, we engineered a tissue engineering polymeric formulation (TEPF) to promote lymphangiogenesis during myocardial repair. The TEPF was fabricated via an integrated strategy combining 3D printing and near-field electrospinning to incorporate 3,4-DHPLA into a biodegradable polyurethane scaffold. The resulting structure mimics the microstructure of the cardiac extracellular matrix while supporting the microenvironment-responsive release of 3,4-DHPLA. RESULTS: We evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of TEPF in rat and porcine ischemia/reperfusion injury models, which markedly improved cardiac function and significantly attenuated adverse ventricular remodeling. Single-cell RNA sequencing and in vitro data further revealed the dual mechanisms of TEPF, not only promoting lymphangiogenesis but also orchestrating a pro-regenerative niche via expansion of Tregs, M2 macrophages, and pro-regenerative fibroblasts (COL12A1+, COL11A1+, NRG1+). CONCLUSIONS: Thus, the tissue engineering polymeric formulations may enable sustained drug release during myocardial tissue repair, thereby alleviating the pain of injection administration for patients with cardiovascular diseases and potentially facilitating patient-friendly use of other functional molecules-based therapeutic tissue engineering formulations through durable delivery.

title: Screening a thermotolerant Komagataella phaffii strain with methanol cross-tolerance and the associated physiological and transcriptional responses.
authors: Li C, Jiang T, Bo Y, Lu Z, Zhou Y, Zhang G
abstract: Komagataella phaffii is a prominent methylotrophic yeast widely used in industrial biotechnology for heterologous protein production, chemical synthesis, and C1 feedstock utilization. However, its industrial application is limited by thermal stress and methanol toxicity, while the relationship between heat adaptation and methanol tolerance remains poorly understood. Here, we obtained a thermotolerant mutant ATH through ARTP mutagenesis followed by adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) under heat stress (37 °C). ATH tolerated heat and methanol robustly under individual stress conditions, achieving 3-fold and 8-fold higher cell densities than GS115 at 37 °C or in 5% (v/v) methanol, respectively, yet failed under the combined stress of 37 °C and 5% methanol. Using three proteins (GFP, OPH, and ChiA) as reporters, we found that ATH showed higher heterologous expression than GS115 at 33 °C. Physiologically, ATH displayed enhanced cell wall/membrane integrity, reduced ROS accumulation and lower lipid peroxidation (>30% reduction in MDA), and accelerated formaldehyde clearance. Transcriptomics identified 561 shared differentially expressed genes, with coordinated upregulation of heat shock proteins (HSP70/40/90 families; Hsp104 and Hsp70-SSA2), antioxidant enzymes (catalase, peroxiredoxin), and cell wall/membrane remodeling genes, alongside downregulation of amino acid and secondary metabolite biosynthesis. Whole-genome resequencing further distinguished ATH from GS115 by only 19 variants (9 SNPs and 10 InDels), highlighting a compact genetic basis for the evolved phenotype. This work provides a K. phaffii chassis with improved individual heat and methanol tolerance and elucidates the physiological, transcriptional, and genomic mechanism underlying heat-methanol cross-adaptation.

title: Cold-induced transcriptomic responses are associated with strain-dependent Salmonella enterica persistence in refrigerated lettuce leaves.
authors: Rodríguez-Alvarez Y, González N, Araya MP, Moreno-Switt AI, Melotto M, Jacob C
abstract: Salmonella enterica is a leading cause of foodborne outbreaks linked to leafy greens. Refrigerated storage is a cornerstone of leafy-green safety, yet strain-level variation in the persistence of internalized S. enterica under these conditions remains poorly understood. Screening of eleven S. enterica strains revealed marked differences in their persistence within detached romaine lettuce leaves stored at 10 °C. Two isolates, belonging to serovars Montevideo and Newport, displaying contrasting persistence phenotypes were selected for detailed analysis, and these differences were confirmed at 4 °C. To investigate transcriptional responses associated with this variation, we profiled transcriptomic responses to cold stress in nutrient-rich medium by RNA-seq and evaluated post-cold recovery. Both isolates grew similarly at 28 °C but diverged at 4 °C, with the Montevideo strain maintaining higher growth capacity. Functional enrichment of KEGG pathways and Gene Ontology terms revealed shared repression of central metabolic and energy-producing pathways, coupled with induction of stress-response processes. Genes associated with general stress responses, cold-shock functions, and envelope integrity were more prominently represented among the induced responses of the Montevideo strain after cold exposure. These findings indicate that strain-dependent differences in Salmonella persistence during refrigerated lettuce storage are associated with distinct transcriptional responses to cold stress and post-cold recovery phenotypes observed in cultured bacteria. Consideration of strain-level variation may improve interpretation of pathogen persistence during leafy-green storage and inform future microbial risk assessments.

title: Identification of Tex and the Phage Shock Protein YthA as putative FtsH substrates associated with the cell envelope stress response in Lactococcus cremoris.
authors: Rendueles C, Escobedo S, Campelo AB, Alonso-Fernández S, Rau MH, Gaspar P, Narberhaus F, Martínez B
abstract: As part of the Cell Envelope Stress (CES) response orchestrated by the two-component system CesSR in lactococci, the FtsH protease is expected to play a role in counteracting stress, as observed in other bacteria. However, neither its specific role nor its substrates have been identified in this genus. The primary objective of this study was therefore to elucidate the FtsH function in the context of CES. A Lactococcus cremoris NZ9000 ΔftsH exhibited an extended lag phase, increased salt and heat sensitivity and lysozyme resistance. However, only the salt and heat sensitive phenotype could be restored by complementation of the ftsH deletion. Whole-genome sequencing revealed putative compensatory mutations in ΔftsH, including genes encoding a transcriptional regulator and components of ABC transporters. Although awaiting experimental validation, these mutations may nevertheless underscore the broader physiological significance of FtsH in L. cremoris. Furthermore, a comparative proteomic analysis of L. cremoris NZ9000 ΔftsH under CES conditions identified putative FtsH substrates. In vivo degradation experiments demonstrated an extended half-life of the RNA-binding protein Tex and the Phage-Shock Protein YthA in a growth-phase dependent manner, thereby proposing these proteins as putative FtsH substrates in L. cremoris. While the specific function of Tex remains to be elucidated, the regulated degradation of YthA suggests that proteolysis may represent an additional regulatory layer within the lactococcal CES response.

title: Aversive learning retroactively modulates neutral episodic memories structured by prior knowledge of predictive sequences.
authors: Baczkowski BM, Villringer A
abstract: Linking memories of temporally separated neutral and threatening experiences can support later recognition of early warning signals. Yet it remains unclear what cognitive processes might allow the seemingly inconsequential neutral events - encoded in safe contexts and thus prone to forgetting - to nevertheless be preserved in memory well enough to inform future threat predictions. Here, we tested whether Pavlovian threat conditioning retroactively strengthens long-term episodic memory for previously encoded neutral events by leveraging prior knowledge of their predictive relations. Young adults first learned to anticipate the order of semantic categories in two deterministic sequences (A → B → C and D → E → F) through repeated presentation of images depicting category exemplars. They then incidentally encoded trial-unique exemplars from each category during sequence viewing. In a next phase, exemplars from the third-position categories were repeated such that one (C) predicted mild electric shocks, whereas the other (F) was never reinforced, creating a category-level threat association through conditioning. After 24 h, recognition memory for exemplars of categories encoded before conditioning depended on sequence and position: when a sequence ended with a shock-predictive category, memory favored the starting category (A) over the following category (B) - an effect absent in the control categories (D and E). These results suggest that aversive learning can retroactively reshape episodic memories of neutral events when they are scaffolded by prior sequence knowledge, bridging temporal gaps and thereby potentially promoting early threat anticipation.

title: Enzymatic cross-linking collagen-based bioink for 3D bioprinting of endometrial model with endometrial epithelial organoids.
authors: Shi H, Xu X, Huang Q, Liu M, Bai X, Ma Y, Wang Y, Lin X
abstract: The human endometrium, a dynamic tissue responsive to sex hormones, plays a pivotal role in female reproduction and menstrual cycling, comprising diverse cell populations including epithelial and stromal cells. The development of in vitro endometrial models holds substantial potential for tissue repair, drug discovery, and disease modeling. However, the construction of biomimetic structural in vitro models capable of supporting long-term culture and preserving relevant biological functions has been hindered by limitations in both material properties and fabrication strategies. Here, an enzymatically cross-linked collagen-based bioink was developed, enabling extrusion bioprinting with favorable printability, biocompatibility, and bioactivity. The enzyme-catalyzed cross-linking process was optimized through room-temperature pre-crosslinking, and its evolution was described using a storage modulus (G')-time kinetic model, enabling prediction of the printable window and reliable fabrication of three-dimensional (3D) constructs. Then, monoculture and co-culture systems of endometrial epithelial organoids (EEOs) and endometrial stromal cells (ESCs) embedded in collagen-based hydrogels were established. Utilizing the bioink and printing strategy, an in vitro endometrial model was 3D bioprinted, exhibiting sustained viability (≥11 days) and hormone-responsive functions comparable to or showing enhanced functional characteristics relative to commonly used Matrigel-based or collagen-based systems. This biomimetic platform provides a physiologically relevant in vitro model for investigating endometrial biology, elucidating pathological mechanisms, and facilitating drug screening applications.

title: Biomimetic sequential targeted nanoplatform for synergistic thrombolysis in ischemic stroke.
authors: Wang J, Wang X, Liu S, Zheng Y, Wang C, Cheng J, Wang X
abstract: Conventional thrombolytic drugs for vascular blockage such as tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) are challenged by the low bioavailability, off-target side effects and limited penetration in thrombi, leading to delayed recanalization. Herein, we developed a sequential targeted nanoplatform for efficient thrombolysis based on the thrombolysis-neuroprotection integrated strategy. The mesoporous silica layer-modified upconversion nanoparticle (UCNP) was loaded with the nitric oxide (NO) donors (BNN6), further coating platelet membranes (PMs) on the surface of UCNP. tPA was conjugated onto PMs using the MMP9-responsive peptide as a linker to form a multifunctional drug carrier of UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA. The proposed drug carrier maintained stability in the blood circulation to reduce bleeding risk (protection), facilitating it colonizing at the thrombus clots. MMP-9 triggered the release of tPA to realize rapid thrombolysis (attack), whereas continuous NO release from NIR-irradiated BNN6 acted to prevent vascular re-embolization (defense). In vitro and in vivo evaluation revealed that UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA enables thrombus-homing accumulation, fluorescence imaging-guided thrombolysis, and NO mediated prevention of thrombosis recurrence, displaying favorable therapeutic outcomes with low bleeding risk. This study offers a facile, safe, and effective way towards the clinical treatment of thrombosis and ischemic stroke.

title: Persistence and epidemiological relevance of Salmonella enterica Newport in public-access waters from a central California coastal agricultural region.
authors: Carter MQ, Carychao D, Gorski L
abstract: Salmonella enterica Newport is one of the most common serotypes linked to fresh produce-associated salmonellosis outbreaks in the United States. In this study, we examined the genetic diversity and epidemiological relevance of 20 Newport strains recovered from Salinas Valley watersheds between 2012 and 2016. Multilocus Sequence Typing (MLST) identified two sequence types (STs), with ST118 representing 70% of isolates and ST45 comprising the remainder. Core-genome MLST (cgMLST) resolved 12 cgSTs, with cgST132506 being the most common. Phenotypic analyses revealed lineage-specific traits, including enhanced biofilm formation and reduced river-water survival in cgST132506 strains. Additionally, ST45 strains adhered significantly better to cantaloupe rind but produced less biofilm on glass surfaces compared with ST118 strains. Epidemiological relevance was assessed by examining matched strains in identified Single Nucleotide Polymorphism (SNP) clusters using the Pathogen Detection pipeline. Two strains were classified as persistent (>500 matches), six as intermediate (50-500), and twelve as transient (<50). Persistent and intermediate strains, considered strains of concern (SOCs), were genomically related to known outbreak strains and widely detected across the United States, including those linked to the 2012 cantaloupe-associated outbreak and the 2017 watermelon-associated outbreak. Although no significant difference in attachment to cantaloupe rind was observed between SOCs and transient strains, SOCs displayed greater river-water survival, while transient strains produced significantly more biofilm. Diverse Newport strains were isolated from the two watersheds examined, and multiple SOCs were recovered from three locations, highlighting the need for targeted investigations into contamination sources in these areas.

title: Feasibility of a Deep-Learning Model for Objective Visualization-Quality Assessment During Cholangioscopy-Guided Lithotripsy: A Proof-of-Concept Study.
authors: Kamada H, Kobayashi K, Yamana H, Fujita N, Namima D, Yamada M, Fujita S, Suto H
abstract: During peroral cholangioscopy-guided electrohydraulic lithotripsy (EHL), stone fragmentation obscures the visual field (the "snowstorm effect"), and visualization quality has been assessed only subjectively. This proof-of-concept study explored the feasibility of a deep-learning method for objectively quantifying visualization quality during EHL and, as an exploratory application, compared viscous gel immersion with saline irrigation. A ResNet-18 model was trained on expert-annotated frames (5-point scale) from three development cases. For independent validation, 120 frames from 12 previously unseen comparison cases were scored by two blinded endoscopists (inter-reader weighted κ = 0.98). The model showed only moderate agreement with their consensus (weighted κ = 0.60; accuracy 70.8%); because the validation sample was enriched for predicted-usable frames, metrics re-weighted to the natural frame distribution gave sensitivity 29.8% and specificity 93.5%, indicating systematic under-detection of usable views. Agreement did not differ systematically between gel and saline frames. The High-Quality View Rate (HQVR) was the proportion of EHL-phase frames scored Good/Excellent. In a patient-level comparison, median HQVR was 22.7% for gel versus 8.4% for saline (exact Mann-Whitney U, p = 0.15, not significant); in post hoc exploratory analyses, a threshold-independent mean predicted score differed (1.65 vs. 1.35, p = 0.005) and the longest continuous usable interval favored gel (median 24.4 vs. 5.2 s). Mild cholangitis occurred in 1/5 gel and 4/7 saline patients. Training such a model is feasible, but it is not yet a validated measurement tool, and the gel-versus-saline signal is hypothesis-generating only. Larger multi-case training and prospective validation are required. Trial Registration: N/A.

title: Benchmarking deep learning-based reconstruction methods for photoacoustic computed tomography with clinically relevant synthetic datasets.
authors: Chen P, Park S, Jeong G, Cam RM, Villa U, Anastasio MA
abstract: SIGNIFICANCE: Deep learning (DL)-based image reconstruction methods for photoacoustic computed tomography (PACT) have developed rapidly in recent years. However, most existing methods have not employed standardized datasets, and their evaluations rely on traditional image quality (IQ) metrics that may lack clinical relevance. The absence of a standardized framework for clinically meaningful IQ assessment hinders fair comparison and raises concerns about the reproducibility and reliability of reported advancements in PACT. AIM: A benchmarking framework is proposed that provides open-source, anatomically plausible synthetic datasets and evaluation strategies for DL-based acoustic inversion methods in PACT. APPROACH: The datasets each include over 10,000 two-dimensional (2D) stochastic breast objects with clinically relevant lesions and paired measurements at varying modeling complexity. The evaluation strategies incorporate both traditional and task-based IQ measures to assess fidelity and clinical utility. A preliminary benchmarking study is conducted to demonstrate the framework's utility by comparing DL-based and physics-based reconstruction methods. RESULTS: The benchmarking study demonstrated that the proposed framework enabled comprehensive, quantitative comparisons of reconstruction performance and revealed important limitations in certain DL-based methods. Although they performed well according to traditional IQ measures, they often failed to accurately recover lesions. This highlights the inadequacy of traditional metrics and motivates the need for task-based assessments. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed benchmarking framework enables systematic comparisons of DL-based acoustic inversion methods for 2D PACT. By integrating clinically relevant synthetic datasets with rigorous evaluation protocols, it enables reproducible, objective assessments and facilitates method development and system optimization in PACT.
